To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed an advanced imaging technique that enables the nondestructive quantitative three-dimensional imaging of whole intact anaerobic ammonox bacteria, and that we have used the technique to study their ultrastructure in relation to their response to environmental changes.

the three-dimensional nondestructively quantitative imaging of the whole anammox bacteria using SXT and TV-SART was achieved for the first time, and the ultrastructure of the intact anoxic bacteria and the shape adaptation to iron were revealed.

quantitative three-dimensional nondestructively imaging of intact anammoxyms bacteria was achieved for the first time, and the results showed that the anammoxosome has a high iron content and that the anammoxyms have a shape adaptation response to iron.

the ultrastructural features of intact anammax bacteria.
the quantitative analysis of the ultrastructural characteristics of anammox bacteria and provides a reference for the study of the morphological structure of other bacteria.

the ultrastructural morphology and the response of anammox bacteria under the influence of different iron levels, which provides new insights into the anammox bacterial ultrastructure and the mechanism of anammox bacterial adaptation to iron.

anammox bacteria have a highly developed intracellular structure and are highly adaptive to their environment, which may provide an explanation for their success in the natural world.
the iron-binding protein is a key factor in maintaining the shape of the anammoxic membrane and the integrity of the anammossome.
the anammoxosome is a unique and distinct organelle, and the shape of the anammoxic bacteria is adapted to iron availability.

the SXT and TV-SART are powerful tools for quantitative three-dimensional ultrastructure imaging of whole anammox bacteria.

the SXT-TV-SART method can be used to obtain the three-dimensional nondestructively ultrastructure of anammox bacteria and to perform a quantitative analysis of anammox cell ultrastructure.
